newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Nat'l Bank could control humane fund gold.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Nat'l Bank could control humane fund gold.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) could end up keeping control of some 400 tonnes of revalued gold reserves the government plans to use to finance a proposed humanitarian foundation, SNB Chairman Hans Meyer said.

As originally proposed by the government last month, the Swiss Solidarity Foundation would get seven billion Swiss francs in revalued gold that would be sold to raise money for victims of poverty, catastrophes and human rights abuses.

"This gold will be converted in steps into interest-bearing assets, so that over the long term average annual revenue of 350 million francs could be expected, which amounts to 50 francs per capita of the population," Meyer said in the text of a speech to be delivered to the central bank's shareholders meeting.
In the past Meyer and other officials have spoken of selling the gold over 10 years to avoid market disruptions.
But Meyer said other variations could finally be adopted, if voters approve the plan in a referendum next year.
"Different solutions are possible in view of a prudent, professional management (of gold) while preserving its substance," he said in the text.

"The 400 tonnes of gold reserves could be transferred to the foundation. But it is also conceivable to leave it on the National Bank's books or to have the National Bank administer it as a trustee," he said.
He did not say whether the other variations also entailed selling the gold on the market.
